topics.label: Introduction to the Cancer Biology Course
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, learning outcomes, and core themes of the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Development and Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics frame cancer as a progressive breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic changes, alongside methods used to model it in vitro.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the pathological hallmarks of tumor invasion and metastasis, using colorectal neoplasia to demonstrate the stepwise progression from benign precursors to invasive malignancy.

topics.label: Tumor Classification, Nomenclature, and Pathological Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the systematic naming conventions for benign and malignant neoplasms and detail the clinical mechanisms through which tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence in Humans and Other Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological frequency and mortality of major cancer types in humans and compare them to tumor patterns across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Cancer Screening and Detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles, histological foundations, and comparative efficacy of early cancer screening programs across different organ systems.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the core learning outcomes and looking ahead to the upcoming practical sessions.
